newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended stronger in active trade on Tuesday, shaking off some nervousness from Monday's Wall Street's 43-point fall in early trade, dealers said.

They said the U.S. market was perceived to have needed a correction and its effect on the local market had been minimal anyway amid upbeat talk of a cut in South African interest rates in the next six months and a fall in the money market shortage. "Our market has been quite healthy and we are expecting it to go better from here," one dealer said.

"Basically I think this is from the positives coming from the currency. Our currency is very, very stable and we've just had some good comment coming from (Reserve Bank Governor Chris) Stals. I just think with the positive news that's been coming out here the market is starting to react.
"People have been holding back on the fears of the Dow and it looks like those kind of fears just seem to be dwindling," he added.
Stals said on Tuesday the Reserve Bank's net oversold position on its forward book had fallen by one billion dollars by March 31, and was expected to fall further as confidence in the rand increased.

He said told Reuters while the central bank was not prepared to comment on the current level of the exchange rate, it welcomed the more stable conditions of the currency over recent months. The rand was last pegged at 4.4465 bid against the U.S. dollar.
The industrial index added 35.7 points to finish at 8,374.5, with dealers saying it still could firm further.

"There is positive stuff coming from the United States, it is not at all in bad shape and I think we've had the correction everyone was anticipating and I think (the market) it's going to stabilise," one dealer said referring to Wall Street's start on Tuesday when it started up 19.66 points.
The dealers said among Tuesday's industrial movers had been Richemont which added 122 cents to finish at 64.75 rand.
Over 1.9 million shares were traded on the stock in a corporate finance deal.
Dealers said interest in Richemont could have been spurred by talk of an early settlement of litigation advances by a number of states against tobacco companies in the United States.
They said also on the movers' list were South African Breweries which shed 75 cents to finish at 131.75 points and Malbak which added 15 cents to 23.15 rand -- with 432,000 shars traded in 126 deals.
Gold shares had started unchanged to finish slightly firmer to mixed on the back of bullion's attempts to hold steady and consolidate its small gains around the $341 an ounce level, dealers said.
The gold index went up 5.7 points to close at 1,263.3, with the yellow metal resisting a fall back to last week's $340 trading level.

"Golds have been slightly better, possibly just consolidating if anything with people sort of perceiving this ($341 level) to be the bottom of the gold price in the short term," one dealer said, adding while the emphasis was on industrials, the financial stocks had also been sought after.
"Banks are quite strong...There is quite a good demand for banks obviously (with the market) expecting good result coming out from most of the banks except one or two," a dealer commented.
First National Bank went up 25 cents to 31.75 rand, Absa up 10 cents to 29.25 rand and NBS added 400 cents to 81.00 rand.
Dealers said Wall Street's Monday's slide had dampened industrial futures while gold contracts heeded bullion's mild up and down rises at the $341 an ounce level.
The June industrial contract closed at 8,211/16 from 8,172 settlement, the golds contract at 885/98 from 891 and the all-share at 6,535/60 from 6,516.
"I see tommorrow being better. I see it follow through from today," one dealer said of the expected market's mood on Wednesday.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom: +27 11 482 1003
